agentCan: Implement the authorization-code flow and token storage
Build Workspace discovery (Get Authorized Teams) and the re-authorization path for missing Workspaces
Handle per-token rate limits with the response headers

approval.trigger: No review of any kind is documented: no app review, approval queue, marketplace/listing submission, or verification step appears in the official API documentation. A Workspace owner/admin creates the app and any user can authorize it immediately.

blockers.detail: ClickUp documents no scope parameter and no scope list: the token inherits everything the authorizing user can access. The only granularity is which Workspaces the user checks on the consent screen. An agent that needs 'read tasks only' cannot express that, and least-privilege arguments that work on other providers do not exist here.
blockers.howToClear: You cannot clear it. Design your data handling around full user-level access and be transparent with customers.
blockers.title: There are no scopes

blockers.detail: Rate limits are per token and set by the AUTHORIZED Workspace's plan: 100 requests/minute on Free Forever, Unlimited, and Business; 1,000/min on Business Plus; 10,000/min on Enterprise. A busy agent connected to a Free-plan customer workspace hits a hard ceiling fast, and the limit follows the customer's plan, not yours.
blockers.howToClear: Read the X-RateLimit headers, back off on 429s, and set customer expectations by plan tier.
blockers.title: Rate limits follow the customer's plan

tested: Read-only verification: app creation location and requirements, the five-step flow, absence of scopes, token behavior, and rate-limit tiers were checked against current developer.clickup.com and help.clickup.com pages (no app created, nothing submitted)
unverified: Whether ClickUp runs any review, verification, or listing program for third-party apps outside the API docs (none appears; no statement either way was found).
Token revocation mechanics for end users and token behavior when a user leaves a Workspace (not stated).
Any limit on OAuth apps per Workspace or users per app (not stated).
Cross-Workspace distribution restrictions (docs describe sending users the connect URL without restriction language, but never address distribution explicitly).

alternatives: Personal API token (pk_...): documented 'for individual or testing purposes' only
flavor.recommended: An OAuth app created inside a ClickUp Workspace (Settings > Apps > Create new app), OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant
flavor.why: It is the only flavor, and the docs are explicit that it is the multi-user route: 'To allow others to use your app, implement the OAuth2 flow so each user has their own token', and 'each user can only access the content available to their individual ClickUp user account'.

humanMust: Be a Workspace owner or admin to create the app
End users choose which Workspaces to grant on the consent screen
name: ClickUp
nuances: 'The access token currently does not expire. This is subject to change.' There is no refresh token; build storage and re-authorization handling as if expiry could arrive.

Calling an endpoint for a Workspace the user did not authorize fails; the documented fix is to send the user through the authorization URL again to modify their selection. Treat missing-Workspace as a normal flow.
Redirect URI matching is host-based: 'the host of the redirect uri must match one of those redirect uris or the request will fail', and non-SSL redirect URIs may lose support in the future.
The app lives in your own Workspace's settings, not a global developer portal; that Workspace's plan and admin context are part of your setup.
The OAuth flow targets the v2 API; 'teams' in API responses are Workspaces.
prerequisites: A ClickUp Workspace where you are owner or admin
A name and at least one redirect URL (use HTTPS)

steps.detail: In your Workspace: avatar > Settings > Apps > Create new app. Enter a name and at least one redirect URL; receive the client_id and secret. Only Workspace owners or admins can do this.
steps.title: Create the app in Workspace settings

steps.detail: Send the user to app.clickup.com/api?client_id={client_id}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri} (optional state). No scope parameter exists to set.
steps.title: Send the user to the authorization URL

steps.detail: On ClickUp's consent screen the user selects one or more Workspaces to grant your app. This selection is ClickUp's permission boundary.
steps.title: User selects Workspaces to grant

steps.detail: The user returns with an authorization code; your backend POSTs to api.clickup.com/api/v2/oauth/token with client_id, client_secret, and code.
steps.title: Exchange the code for a token

steps.detail: Call the API with Authorization: Bearer {access_token}. Use GET /api/v2/team (Get Authorized Teams) to discover which Workspaces the token may access; to add Workspaces later, send the user through the authorization URL again.
steps.title: Call the API and discover Workspaces

tagline: The five-step OAuth flow: create an app inside a Workspace, send users to one URL, exchange a code. No review, no listing, and remarkably, no scopes: the token is the user's full access, bounded only by which Workspaces they select.

time.active: ~5 min of setup + under an hour of flow code
time.total: Same day; nothing to wait for
